alt: A curve of the pen's area for every whole side length x. The peak of the parabola is marked at w over 4. The whole numbers on either side of it are the only candidates, and the larger of the two areas is the answer. In one preset a limit on x moves the best choice to the end of the allowed range.

steps.caption: 21 meters of wire fence a rectangle against a long wall. Two sides of length x and one of length 21 - 2x need wire, so the area is x * (21 - 2x). Each x from 1 to 10 is one case; the curve shows them all.
Area is -2x^2 + 21x, a parabola that opens downward, so its peak is at x = 21/4 = 5.25. Whole numbers only, so the peak is not always a case.
The two whole numbers beside the peak, 5 and 6, are the only candidates. Their areas: 55 at x = 5, 54 at x = 6. The larger is 55 at x = 5.

22 meters of wire fence a rectangle against a long wall. Two sides of length x and one of length 22 - 2x need wire, so the area is x * (22 - 2x). Each x from 1 to 10 is one case; the curve shows them all.
Area is -2x^2 + 22x, a parabola that opens downward, so its peak is at x = 22/4 = 5.5. Whole numbers only, so the peak is not always a case.
The two whole numbers beside the peak, 5 and 6, are the only candidates. Their areas tie at 60, so x = 5 stays.

40 meters of wire fence a rectangle against a long wall. Two sides of length x and one of length 40 - 2x need wire, so the area is x * (40 - 2x). Each x from 1 to 19 is one case; the curve shows them all.
A shed restricts x to at most 6. The shaded band is the allowed range; cases to its right are off the table.
Area is -2x^2 + 40x, a parabola that opens downward, so its peak is at x = 40/4 = 10. Whole numbers only, so the peak is not always a case.
The peak at 10 lies beyond the allowed range, so the clamp pulls both candidates to x = 6. Both land on x = 6, area 168.
